The season that comes after autumn is winter.

To understand the concept of encryption described in the content, we can compare it to the familiar idea of a sealed envelope. When you write a private letter, you place it in an envelope and seal it. Anyone can see the envelope and handle it during transit, but they cannot read the message inside because the paper is opaque and the seal is intact. Only the person who receives the envelope and has the permission (or key) to open it can read the contents. Similarly, encryption scrambles data so that it looks like gibberish to anyone who intercepts it, ensuring that only the intended recipient, who possesses the correct decryption key, can "open" the data and understand the original message. This analogy helps illustrate how confidentiality is maintained without needing to hide the existence of the communication itself.
